tagline: Type each third-party key once on the studio; the vault hands it only to the projects you've granted it to.
summary: Env Vault is a self-built credential vault for vendor keys such as `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `GITHUB_TOKEN`. You enter each value once in the admin UI. The vault then delivers it to gateway-spawned workers and to API/storage servers started by Luckee Hub, with a managed `.env` block as a last resort. Nobody copies keys between `.env` files anymore.

A key reaches a project only when the project requests it **and** a person has granted it. Values are encrypted with AES-256-GCM under keys held in the macOS Keychain, and `resolve` is reachable only over a `0600` Unix domain socket. Status: design is done (`docs/vault/`); Phase 1 (vault core) hasn't started, so both repos are still the starter templates.
audience: You run several Luckee projects on the studio and are tired of copying vendor keys into each `.env`.
You want to see in Hub which keys each project needs and whether they're set.
notFor: Platform/runtime secrets (`*_DISPATCHER_*`, `STORAGE_SECRET`) or non-secrets like `PORT`. Only vendor keys.
Replacing it with 1Password, Doppler, HashiCorp Vault or Infisical. Building our own is a final decision.
Remote access. Values never leave the studio over TCP.

capabilities.title: Write-only key entry
capabilities.detail: Add and rotate values in env-vault-web; values are versioned from day one (planned, Phase 2).

capabilities.title: Per-project grants
capabilities.detail: `resolve(project, names)` returns only requested ∩ granted names; the rest are reported as `not_granted` / `missing`, names only (planned, Phase 1).

capabilities.title: Audit log
capabilities.detail: Every resolve, grant, revoke, put, rotate, reveal, export and unlock is logged, never with a value (planned).

capabilities.title: Encrypted backup
capabilities.detail: `export` writes a bundle re-wrapped under a recovery key shown once at setup (planned).

capabilities.title: Hub key status
capabilities.detail: Hub shows which vendor keys each project needs, whether they're set, and how they're delivered (planned; see `05-luckee-hub-status.md`).

components.name: Vault core
components.runsOn: The studio (Hub port 3101 for health/admin only)
components.owns: Encrypted secret storage, grants, the audit log, `resolve` over the Unix socket, backup/restore.
components.doesNotOwn: The admin UI, or deciding which keys a project requests.

components.name: Admin UI
components.owns: Adding/rotating keys (write-only), grants per project, audit log view, backup export, lock/unlock.
components.doesNotOwn: Secret values: it never receives one back.

dataFlow: You enter a key in env-vault-web; it goes to the vault over the local admin channel and is stored encrypted.
You grant the key to one or more projects.
When Hub or the gateway starts a project, it calls `resolve` over the Unix socket with the names the project requests and injects only the granted values into the child environment.

trust.title: Browser
trust.detail: Never sees a stored value. Reveal requires fresh re-auth.

trust.title: Vault
trust.detail: Holds ciphertext; data keys are wrapped by a key in the macOS Keychain. No TCP listener returns values.

trust.title: Projects
trust.detail: Receive only keys they requested and a person granted.

troubleshooting.fix: The web `.env.example` still points at 3009; Hub Run injects `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` for port 3101.

glossary.definition: A person's approval for one project to receive one key. Requesting a key never grants it.
The socket-only call that returns granted values to a process being started.

hubNotes: Both repos are still starter templates; Run only gives you the health endpoint and a blank page.
Repos live at `~/github/env-vault/`, outside the `luckee/` folder.
Per the threat model, the Express port must stay health/admin only. `resolve` belongs on the Unix socket.
